title: Database Administrators
description: Administer, test, and implement computer databases, applying knowledge of database management systems. Coordinate changes to computer databases. Identify, investigate, and resolve database performance issues, database capacity, and database scalability. May plan, coordinate, and implement security measures to safeguard computer databases.

tasks.text: Modify existing databases and database management systems or direct programmers and analysts to make changes.
Plan, coordinate, and implement security measures to safeguard information in computer files against accidental or unauthorized damage, modification or disclosure.
Plan and install upgrades of database management system software to enhance database performance.
Specify users and user access levels for each segment of database.
Test changes to database applications or systems.
Test programs or databases, correct errors, and make necessary modifications.
Provide technical support to junior staff or clients.
Approve, schedule, plan, and supervise the installation and testing of new products and improvements to computer systems, such as the installation of new databases.
Develop standards and guidelines for the use and acquisition of software and to protect vulnerable information.
Write and code logical and physical database descriptions and specify identifiers of database to management system, or direct others in coding descriptions.
Develop data models describing data elements and how they are used, following procedures and using pen, template, or computer software.
Select and enter codes to monitor database performance and to create production databases.
Identify, evaluate and recommend hardware or software technologies to achieve desired database performance.
Review procedures in database management system manuals to make changes to database.
Identify and evaluate industry trends in database systems to serve as a source of information and advice for upper management.
Review workflow charts developed by programmer analyst to understand tasks computer will perform, such as updating records.
Revise company definition of data as defined in data dictionary.

skills.name: Critical Thinking

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Programming
skills.def: Writing computer programs for various purposes.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Operations Analysis
skills.def: Analyzing needs and product requirements to create a design.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud EC2, Amazon Redshift, Amazon Web Services AWS software, Apache Hive.

skills.name: Data base management system software
skills.def: Software to store, organize, or provide access to a set of related information. Examples: ADO.NET, Amazon Data Pipeline, Amazon DynamoDB, Apache Cassandra.

skills.name: Development environment software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications which run on a computer or mobile device. Examples: Apache Ant, Apache Kafka, Apache Maven, C.

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: Advanced business application programming ABAP, Apache Groovy, C#, C++.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Apple macOS, Bash, DOS shell script, Hewlett Packard HP-UX.

skills.name: Business intelligence and data analysis software
skills.def: Software to present, visualize, or analyze data to help businesses make informed decisions. Examples: Apache Spark, IBM Cognos Impromptu, Micosoft SQL Server Analysis Services SSAS, Microsoft Power BI.
